advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Broaden `_offending_source` to also match bare `O_CREAT` (word-boundary) so a copy using `from os import O_CREAT` cannot evade the anti-duplication guard.
evidence: src/rebar/_store/stamped_lock.py:119: `if "os.O_CREAT" not in text or "stamped_file_is_stale" not in text:`
The docstring frames the anchor as "the CONJUNCTION of ``os.O_CREAT`` and ``stamped_file_is_stale``" but matches only the dotted spelling, missing `from os import O_CREAT` / bare `O_CREAT` usages.
src/rebar/_store/stamped_lock.py:122-125: presence of any marker returns `None` (no offence) for the whole file regardless of where the O_CREAT/stale conjunction sits.
advisory.finding: The construct-uniqueness guard `_offending_source` keys on the literal substring `os.O_CREAT`, so a fourth copy that imports the flag differently (e.g. `from os import O_CREAT` and uses bare `O_CREAT`, or `oflags = os.O_CREAT | ...` aliased) would not be flagged, letting the copy re-enter undetected — the exact drift the guard exists to prevent.
merged_from: `_offending_source` searches for the `# stamped-lock-ok:` marker anywhere in the whole file text, so a single reasoned marker suppresses ALL stamped-lock acquires in that module, not just the one it annotates — a second, unsanctioned copy added later to a module that already carries one blessed exception would be silently exempted.
advisory.suggested_fix: Match a word-boundary `O_CREAT` (regex `\bO_CREAT\b`) rather than the literal `os.O_CREAT` substring, keeping the conjunction with `stamped_file_is_stale`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the exact-substring-count assertions in test_the_unrelated_o_excl_uses_survive with an assertion that _offending_source returns None for each of those files (the behavior the guard actually protects), rather than counting 'O_EXCL' occurrences including prose.
evidence: src/rebar/_store/fsutil.py:13: `unique, ``O_EXCL`` name) in the SAME directory as ``path`` and published with` — the counted O_EXCL is prose, not executable code

The real consolidation invariant is enforced by test_the_stamped_lock_acquire_appears_only_in_its_owner (conjunction anchor) which already has positive control test_the_scan_flags_a_copied_acquire and negative control test_the_scan_ignores_a_reader_and_an_unrelated_create; this count-table test adds fragility on prose without adding behavioral coverage.
advisory.finding: test_the_unrelated_o_excl_uses_survive asserts exact per-file counts of the substring 'O_EXCL' across five source files, including occurrences in prose/docstrings (e.g. _store/fsutil.py's only 'O_EXCL' is inside a docstring, confirmed at fsutil.py:13). This is a change-detector: a behavior-preserving edit (rewording a docstring that mentions O_EXCL, or adding an unrelated exclusive create in keyprov.py) breaks the test with no observable-behavior change, and it duplicates the invariant already enforced (with its own positive/negative unit tests) by the O_CREAT+stamped_file_is_stale conjunction guard.
scenarios: A future PR rewords a docstring mentioning O_EXCL in one of the five listed files.
keyprov.py gains a second unrelated O_EXCL create.
advisory.suggested_fix: For each listed file assert `_offending_source((_SRC_REBAR / rel).read_text()) is None` instead of counting O_EXCL substrings, so the test survives docstring rewording and unrelated exclusive creates while still proving the guard leaves legitimate uses alone.
